## We Specialize In

Pet Emergency Care & Oncology in North Little Rock

At After Hour Animal Hospital, we provide emergency and specialized care for dogs and cats in Central Arkansas, including compassionate oncology services.

As a full-service veterinary emergency facility, we're equipped to handle your pet’s urgent needs with advanced diagnostics, a fully stocked in-house pharmacy, and around-the-clock staff. Our in-house lab delivers fast results, and we offer digital radiology, ultrasound, and endoscopy to support accurate, timely diagnoses. We also maintain critical emergency supplies such as snake antivenom and transfusion products.

For pets facing a cancer diagnosis, we’re proud to offer specialized oncology care with a focus on collaboration, clear communication, and tailored treatment plans. Whether we’re managing an urgent injury or providing ongoing support for a serious illness, our team is committed to delivering expert, compassionate care when your pet needs it most.

#### Jessica Mobley

DVM, DACVIM (Oncology)

Dr. Jessica Mobley grew up in the suburbs of Atlanta and is a proud SEC graduate, having attended the University of Georgia for her undergraduate studies, veterinary school, and specialty residency (Go Dawgs!). After veterinary school, she completed a small animal rotating internship at North Carolina State University in 2013, then returned to Athens for her medical oncology residency. She became a Diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine – Medical Oncology in 2016.
Dr. Mobley started a medical oncology service in Atlanta, where she practiced for the last eight years, and also helped establish other medical oncology services in Florida and Illinois. She currently serves as the Chair of Medical Initiatives for Thrive’s Medical Excellence and Education Department.
She is excited to be in the beautiful Natural State of Arkansas, providing cancer diagnostics and treatments for pets and their families!

Read Full Bio

#### Mark E. Sharp

DVM, CCRT - Medical Director

Dr. Sharp was born and raised on a farm in Muldrow, OK. He graduated from the Oklahoma State University College of Veterinary Medicine in 2001 and began practicing at South County Animal Hospital as an associate. In March 2002, he took over ownership of the hospital, which he has led since 2017. Dr. Sharp’s primary interests include referral orthopedics and neurosurgery. A lover of technology, he is continually seeking innovative ways to advance veterinary medicine. In 2015, he opened a referral-only practice in Fayetteville, Arkansas (Advanced Veterinary Surgery and Rehabilitation Center) focused on orthopedic surgery and neurosurgery. Outside of work, Dr. Sharp enjoys traveling and spending time with family and friends. His primary hobby is physical exercise.

Your Role as a Veterinary Oncologist 

As a vital member of our Oncology team, you'll play a hands-on role in diagnosing, treating, and managing cancer in veterinary patients, utilizing advanced therapies including surgery, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and other specialized treatments. You'll develop and oversee individualized treatment plans, collaborate closely with primary care veterinarians and our multidisciplinary team, and communicate compassionately with pet owners throughout their pet's cancer journey. You'll build and manage a diverse oncology caseload, utilize state-of-the-art diagnostic and treatment technology, and contribute to the continued growth of our oncology service through education, collaboration, and exceptional patient care. This position is ideal for a compassionate, highly skilled, and curious individual who thrives in a collaborative environment and is passionate about providing advanced cancer care while making a meaningful difference for pets and the people who love them.

 
You’ll use your expertise to:
-Provide advanced oncology care in accordance with ACVIM guidelines, establishing and managing a strong caseload while delivering compassionate, ethical, and high-quality patient care.
-Collaborate with specialists, emergency doctors, technicians, referring veterinarians, and clients to develop individualized treatment plans and ensure comprehensive care and follow-up.
-Maintain accurate and timely medical records, treatment plans, and client estimates while balancing each patient’s medical needs with the client’s financial considerations.
-Lead, mentor, and support oncology technicians and technician assistants while actively participating in hospital rounds, department meetings, team-building activities, and continuing education.
-Contribute to the growth of the Oncology service through community outreach, Lunch & Learns, marketing events, and ongoing relationship-building with referring veterinary practices.

 
Requirements 

Required:

Colorado Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) License.
Board Certification through ACVIM.
Registration with DORA.
AVMA PLIT Insurance.
DEA License. 

Schedule 
Specialty doctors are expected to work 4 x 10-hour shifts alongside their department medical team. Hours and days dependent on case load and overall needs of the hospital. Further schedule details will be discussed and outlined in the contract for employment agreement. 

 
Work Environment & Physical Demands 

This role is physically active and fast-paced. You’ll need to: 

Lift up to 50 lbs frequently 
Kneel, stoop, crouch, and be on your feet for long periods 
Operate medical and office equipment 
Work around biological hazards and cleaning agents 
Communicate clearly in noisy environments 
About EVS 

Mission: To provide elevated specialty and emergency veterinary care, fostering a compassionate and collaborative environment that supports pets and the people who care for them.
